_note: Frozen content for design review. Phosphor family — scan lines as the ground texture, wide registers alternating in tone, one lit per page. No terminal chrome, no prompts, no monospace body copy.
brief: Debugging as a discipline applied to things that are not code

slots.eyebrow: On finding out what is actually wrong
slots.standfirst: Six habits taken from debugging and pointed at a stuck project, a bad hire, a launch that underperformed.
slots.item1: Why the first explanation is almost never the cause
slots.item2: The one question that ends a circular argument
slots.coverNote: The last page is the reason most investigations stop too early

slots.body: Most of the effort goes into theories about a thing that has happened once. Until you can make it happen on purpose you have no way to tell a fix from a coincidence, and every change after that point is superstition with a deployment attached.
slots.v1: Deliberately, from a known start. Nothing before this counts as evidence.
slots.v2: The exact conditions, not the summary. The summary is where the detail dies.
slots.v3: An unreproducible problem is a different problem and needs a different plan.

slots.body: Shipping three fixes together and watching the number recover tells you that one of them worked, which you already assumed. The instinct to do everything at once comes from urgency, and urgency is exactly when you can least afford an uninterpretable result.
slots.v1: Slower per round and far faster to an actual answer.
slots.v2: Otherwise you are testing combinations you never intended to build.
slots.v3: What you changed, what happened. Nobody remembers round four correctly.

slots.body: Faced with forty possible causes, most people start at the one they find most interesting. Cutting the space in half repeatedly reaches the answer in six steps regardless of where it is, and it works even when you have no intuition at all.
slots.v1: Any split that rules out half is worth more than a clever guess.
slots.v2: Elimination survives being wrong about which half you expected.
slots.v3: It is unsatisfying right until the step where it lands on the cause.

slots.body: What somebody tells you happened has already been through their interpretation of it, and the interpretation is where the useful detail was lost. Going to the raw thing — the log, the recording, the original message — almost always contradicts the summary in one specific way.
slots.v1: One layer of retelling is enough to remove the decisive detail.
slots.v2: The part everybody quotes is rarely the part that matters.
slots.v3: The thing that should be there and is not is the strongest clue available.

slots.body: The search stops at the boundary of what you consider impossible, which is why difficult problems live exactly there. When every candidate is exhausted the honest next step is to verify something you have never once checked because it obviously works.
slots.v1: Out loud. The list is shorter and stranger than you expect.
slots.v2: Clock, spelling, permission, whether it is even running at all.
slots.v3: Every time the word appears you have stopped looking at something.

slots.body: A story that explains the symptom feels identical to the cause, and the relief of having one ends the search. The test is whether you can use the explanation to make the problem come back on demand, and most explanations that get shipped cannot.
slots.v1: A story that fits and a cause that predicts are different objects.
slots.v2: If the explanation is right you can turn the fault on and off at will.
slots.v3: An explanation with no failing case is a preference, not a finding.

slots.eyebrow: On the thing nobody has got to the bottom of
slots.body: Take the recurring problem everybody has a theory about and try to cause it deliberately. Whether you can is more informative than any of the theories.
slots.closingLine: If you cannot turn it on, you cannot claim to have turned it off.
